notes: Broad search for moral psychology benchmarking papers relevant to LLMs, focusing on underrepresented theories and non-Western moral frameworks. 12 primary queries + 16 follow-up queries. Cross-referenced against 2,043 vault papers and 29 results from v1 search (20260403-external-search-merged.json).

results.title: The Fragility of Moral Judgment in Large Language Models
results.notes: 2,939 dilemmas from r/AmItheAsshole. 3 perturbation families: surface edits (7.5% flip), POV shifts (24.3% flip), persuasion cues. Protocol choice dominates (only 67.6% agreement). Tests dual-process-adjacent stability. 4 models (GPT-4.1, Claude 3.7, DeepSeek V3, Qwen2.5-72B), 129K judgments. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Moral Sycophancy in Vision Language Models
results.notes: Tests moral sycophancy in VLMs -- moral stances flip under user disagreement, with morally-right-to-wrong transitions more frequent than reverse. Relevant to social intuitionism: tests whether models capitulate to social pressure rather than maintaining moral judgments. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Visual Distraction Undermines Moral Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
results.notes: Introduces Moral Dilemma Simulation (MDS) benchmark grounded in MFT. Visual inputs bypass text-based safety, activating 'System 1-like' intuitive processing. VLMs lose sensitivity to numerical stakes, prioritize self-interest, collapse hierarchical social values. Directly tests dual-process theory predictions in multimodal setting. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Decoding Moral Responses in AI: A Quantitative Analysis of Large Language Models
results.authors: Hendra et al. (City University of Hong Kong)
results.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans (Elsevier)
results.notes: Compares 7 LLMs (GPT-3/3.5/4/4.1, Claude 3.7, Grok 3, Gemini 2.5 Pro) on moral dilemmas. Finds LLMs more utilitarian in impersonal dilemmas (dual-process prediction). Few-shot = slow thinking; fast-thinking is a blind spot. Advocates 'AI Psychology' as new field. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Insights into Moral Reasoning of AI: A Comparative Study Between Humans and Large Language Models
results.notes: Comparative study of human vs LLM moral reasoning. Published in media ethics journal. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Moral Disagreement and the Limits of AI Value Alignment: A Dual Challenge of Epistemic Justification and Political Legitimacy
results.notes: Argues crowdsourcing, RLHF, and constitutional AI all fail to accommodate reasonable moral disagreement. When AI operates at governance scale, must satisfy public justification norms. Directly relevant to pluralistic moral evaluation. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Ethical Pluralism in AI: Challenging the Monolithic Values of Red Teams
results.notes: Critiques red team ethical reductionism where AI outputs reflect narrow values. Proposes user-driven ethical configurations and distributed oversight. Directly relevant to adversarial moral evaluation and pluralistic benchmarking. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Islamic Ethics and AI: An Evaluation of Existing Approaches to AI using Trusteeship Ethics
results.notes: Introduces Taha Abdurrahman's I'timani (trusteeship) framework for AI. Three covenants: Ontological, Epistemological, Existential. Critiques Western procedural ethics (Floridi) and Maqasid/Qawaid approaches. Argues for spiritual accountability in AI governance. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Al-Ghazali's Principle of Trust (Amanah) as a Framework for Ethical AI Governance in Organizations
results.notes: Applies Al-Ghazali's Amanah (trust) principle to AI governance. Integrates justice (adl), trust (amanah), communal benefit (maslahah). NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: The Virtue of Artificiality: Islamic Ethics and the Reconceptualization of AI Caregivers
results.notes: Introduces 'neutragents' concept -- AI caregivers transcend mahram/non-mahram dichotomy in Islamic care ethics. Artificiality uniquely aligns with Islamic ethics. Implications for intercultural value alignment. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Islamic Virtue-Based Ethics for Artificial Intelligence
results.notes: Islamic virtue-based AI ethics grounded in Maqasid. Tazkiya (self-purification) as overarching goal. Alternative to Western ethical frameworks. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Maqasid Al-Shariah in the Age of AI: A Critical Examination
results.notes: Critical examination of Maqasid al-Shariah applied to AI. Five essential protections (daruriyyat): faith, life, intellect, lineage, wealth. Notes Islamic AI ethics still dominated by normative/declarative approaches. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Ethics of AI in Africa: Interrogating the Role of Ubuntu and AI Governance Initiatives
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Yilma-Ethics of AI in Africa.md). Systematic review of Ubuntu-centered AI ethics. 9 recurrent themes: communal data stewardship, collective responsibility, contextual fairness, ecological sustainability, intersectionality. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: AI Ethics Meets Ubuntu: Towards a Context-Aware Governance Model for Sustainable Innovation in Africa
results.venue: IJSRM (International Journal of Scientific Research and Management)
results.notes: Five-layer Ubuntu governance architecture for AI: Community Data Trusts, Relational Design Praxis, Harm Reconciliation Panels, Ecological Stewardship Protocols, Developer Benefit Realisation. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Indigenous Ethics and Artificial Intelligence
results.notes: Indigenous ethics of reciprocity as normative and epistemological framework. Challenges Western linear conceptions. Reciprocity as vital principle of survival, not mere exchange. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Indigenous Peoples and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review and Future Directions
results.authors: Perera, Vidanaarachchi, Chandrashekeran, Kennedy, Kennedy, Halgamuge
results.notes: Systematic review of Indigenous peoples and AI. Covers data sovereignty, decolonizing algorithms, cultural sensitivity. ML health models showed biased predictions for Maori patients. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Dharma in the Digital Age: Some Reflections on Buddhism and Artificial Intelligence
results.venue: In: Mind, Text, and Reality in Buddhist Studies (book chapter)
results.notes: Scholarly reflections on Buddhism and AI. Broader ethical concerns about AI alignment with Buddhist nonviolence and alleviation of suffering. Published in academic volume. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Can a Machine Flow Like Dao? The Daoist Philosophy on Artificial Intelligence
results.venue: Springer (book chapter in Asian Philosophies and the Idea of Religion)
results.notes: Daoist philosophical analysis of AI. Wu-wei (non-action) applied to technology design. Considers AI and robotics as potential 'companions' in Confucian/Daoist cosmology. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Faith, Ethics, and Human Dignity in an Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Call to Action
results.authors: Multi-faith coalition (Church of Jesus Christ et al.)
results.venue: Newsroom (Church of Jesus Christ) / Multi-faith summit
results.notes: Multi-faith, multi-university AI auditing tool. 7 evaluation categories. Faith Community AI Evaluation (FACE) tool. 2026 Vatican conference planned. Pluralistic religious AI benchmarking initiative -- the closest thing to a religious values AI benchmark. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: How Much of a Pluralist is ChatGPT? A Comparative Study of Value Pluralism in Generative AI Chatbots
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-SOCIETY-How Much of a Pluralist is.md). Magic Wand Survey (MWS). 2 dimensions: Both/and Reasoning + Willingness to Preserve Difference. 4 chatbots vs N=335 humans. Chatbots higher cognitive but lower behavioral pluralism. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: The Value of Disagreement in AI Design, Evaluation, and Alignment
results.notes: Examines disagreement as productive for AI design and evaluation. FAccT paper on value pluralism in alignment. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: AI Red-Teaming is a Sociotechnical Challenge: On Values, Labor, and Harms
results.notes: Critiques red teaming as lacking sociocultural, historical, legal, ethical proficiencies. Incentive structures don't reward such expertise. Relevant to adversarial moral reasoning evaluation. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Sacred Values and LLM-Generated Persuasion
results.notes: Study with N=951 Democrats/Republicans. LLM-generated arguments appealing to rights/fairness increase willingness to fight/die for political stances, mediated by perceiving stance as having absolute (sacred) value. Directly tests sacred values psychology + LLM persuasion. URL not directly confirmed. NOT IN VAULT.

results.title: Moral Judgment of LLM Using Korean Datasets and Eastern Ethical Principles
results.venue: Annual Conference of KIPS (Korea Information Processing Society)
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Yoo-Moral Judgment of LLM Using Korean Datasets and Eastern Ethical.md). Evaluates LLMs on Korean moral datasets with Eastern ethical principles. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Cross-Cultural Value Alignment Frameworks for Responsible AI Governance: Evidence from China-West Comparative Analysis
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Liu-Cross-cultural value alignment frameworks.md). Multi-Layered Auditing Platform for Responsible AI. Evaluates 20+ models (Qwen, GPT-4o, Claude, LLaMA, DeepSeek). ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Do Large Language Models Understand Morality Across Cultures?
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Mohammadi-Do Large Language Models Understand Morality Across Cultures.md). Tests LLM understanding of morality across cultures. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: A Dual-Layered Evaluation of Geopolitical and Cultural Bias in LLMs
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Kim-A Dual-Layered Evaluation of Geopolitical and Cultural Bias in LLMs.md). Evaluates geopolitical and cultural bias in LLMs. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Assessing LLMs for Moral Value Pluralism
results.notes: IN VAULT (2023-Benkler-Assessing LLMs for Moral Value Pluralism.md). Dedicated assessment of moral value pluralism in LLMs. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Comparing Moral Values in Western English-speaking Countries
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Xiang-Comparing Moral Values in Western.md). Compares moral values in Western English-speaking countries. Relevant baseline but Western-focused. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Diagnosing Moral Reasoning Acquisition in Language Models
results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Liu-Diagnosing Moral Reasoning Acquisition in.md). Tests how moral reasoning is acquired during LLM training. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.notes: IN VAULT (2025-Tennant-Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025 MORAL ALIGNMENT FOR LLM.md). Uses intrinsic moral rewards for automated alignment. ALREADY INGESTED.

results.title: Democratizing Value Alignment: From Authoritarian to Democratic AI Ethics
results.notes: Argues for democratizing value alignment. When AI operates at scale = governance. Must satisfy public justification standards. NOT IN VAULT.

key_findings.non_western_coverage: Significant gap confirmed. Found 14 papers engaging non-Western moral frameworks (Islamic, Ubuntu, Indigenous, Buddhist, Daoist, Confucian) but NONE are computational benchmarks. All are theoretical/normative frameworks. The closest to an operationalized evaluation is the Faith Community AI Evaluation (FACE) multi-faith auditing tool and the Korean Eastern Ethical Principles evaluation (already in vault).
key_findings.islamic_ethics: 5 papers found spanning trusteeship ethics (I'timani), Al-Ghazali's Amanah, virtue-based ethics, Maqasid al-Shariah, and AI caregivers. All are philosophical frameworks, not computational benchmarks. The Islamic AI ethics field is normative/declarative, with limited operationalization.
key_findings.ubuntu_and_african: 2 new papers on Ubuntu AI ethics (Springer Ethics & Information Technology; IJSRM). Ubuntu defines fairness as restoration of communal harmony, not statistical equivalence. No benchmark operationalizing Ubuntu exists.
key_findings.indigenous_ethics: 2 new papers: systematic review (Perera et al., SAGE) and indigenous ethics framework (Springer). Data sovereignty and decolonizing algorithms are key themes. No computational benchmark.
key_findings.buddhist_and_daoist: 1 Buddhist (Dharma in the Digital Age) + 1 Daoist (Can a Machine Flow Like Dao). Both philosophical, no benchmarks. NORBU Buddhist AI project already in vault.
key_findings.adversarial_moral_reasoning: 4 papers found. Key: Schuster & Kilov (RLHF/constitutional AI fail on moral disagreement), Ethical Pluralism in AI (red team monolithic values), AI Red-Teaming sociotechnical challenge, and Value of Disagreement (FAccT 2025). The adversarial moral reasoning space is growing but focused on alignment critique rather than benchmark creation.
key_findings.moral_robustness_benchmarks: 3 new papers on moral fragility/robustness: van Nuenen & Sachdeva (perturbation framework, 129K judgments), Moral Sycophancy in VLMs, and Visual Distraction Undermines Moral Reasoning (MDS benchmark). These are highly relevant to dual-process theory testing.
key_findings.sacred_values: Near zero dedicated benchmarks. Found 1 study connecting LLM-generated persuasion to sacred value psychology (N=951, political stances). Tetlock's taboo trade-off paradigm has NOT been operationalized for LLM evaluation.
key_findings.dual_process_update: v2 search found 3 additional dual-process-relevant papers beyond v1: Moral Fragility (perturbation robustness), Visual Distraction MDS (multimodal dual-process), Decoding Moral Responses (7 LLMs, utilitarian bias in impersonal dilemmas).
gap_severity_ranking: 1. Sacred Values / Taboo Trade-offs -- ZERO benchmarks
2. Social Intuitionism / Moral Dumbfounding -- ZERO dedicated benchmarks (confirmed by v1 search; v2 found only tangential VLM sycophancy)
3. Dyadic Morality -- ZERO dedicated benchmarks (confirmed by v1 search)
4. Non-Western frameworks (Islamic/Ubuntu/Buddhist/Daoist/Indigenous) -- frameworks exist but ZERO computational benchmarks
5. Adversarial moral reasoning -- growing critique literature but few evaluation tools
6. Dual Process Theory -- best covered but still no benchmark explicitly citing Greene's framework
